name: Ceramic braces

lead: Ceramic braces use tooth-coloured brackets with a wire to straighten teeth, aiming to be less visible than metal.
Research is mostly surveys and lab studies.

paras: Same as other fixed braces: steady wire pressure moves teeth as bone remodels.
Fixed appliances raise plaque and Candida colonisation; lab work examines enamel micro-cracks on debonding.

lead: Ceramic braces are fixed orthodontic appliances whose brackets are tooth-coloured rather than metal, designed to be less noticeable than traditional metal braces. They work like other fixed braces, using brackets and an archwire to apply pressure that moves teeth [1].

Research includes comparisons of microbial adhesion on metal, ceramic and self-ligating brackets in vitro [2], surveys of how adults weigh aesthetics when choosing appliances [3], and a study of appliance type and hiring prospects [4].

paras: Ceramic and clear aligners are described as cosmetic options compared with traditional metallic braces [4]. Adult patients reportedly want discreet appliances, but the factors shaping their choice are still poorly understood [3].

A cross-sectional study photographed models with metal braces, ceramic braces and clear aligners to examine effects on job-hiring prospects in Saudi Arabia [4]. A 2025 study compared oral-health-related quality of life in adults with ceramic braces versus aligners [5].

Fixed appliances are associated with increased Candida colonisation in a prospective controlled trial [6]. In vitro studies have examined biofilm formation on bracket types [2], salivary pH effects of different appliances [7], and enamel micro-cracks and debonding of ceramic brackets after thermocycling [8].

A prospective controlled trial found fixed orthodontic appliances change oral microbiota including Candida colonisation [6]. A survey study compared quality of life with ceramic braces and aligners [5]. Other findings are laboratory-based [2][8][7].
